html:
Ruhollah Khomeini was a Shia cleric who led the Iranian Revolution of 1979 and ruled the new Islamic Republic of Iran as its Supreme Leader until his death in 1989. His birth date is given as 1900 or 1902.

A teacher of law and mysticism in Qom, he became famous in 1963 by attacking the White Revolution reforms of Mohammad Reza Shah and the Shah's ties to the United States. He was exiled in 1964 and lived in Iraq and then France. From Najaf he taught that a qualified jurist should rule in the absence of the hidden Imam.

Cassette tapes of his sermons spread through Iran. When mass protests forced the Shah out, Khomeini returned in February 1979 to huge crowds. He set up clerical rule, purged opponents, backed the seizure of the US embassy and led Iran through the long war with Iraq. In 1989 he issued a fatwa calling for the death of the novelist Salman Rushdie.
